# Round 6 — REQ-X coverage register (exact supplemental ownership)

**Status:** decomposition draft, revised after the Phase-4 split review (SR-1…SR-27; see the [plan's review record](2026-11-07_round6-decomposition.md#phase-4-review-record-2026-11-07)), then regenerated for the operator's re-partition of 2026-11-07 (128 → 73 rows, 97 → 48 implement-spec, 3-run tail; see the [plan's re-partition record](2026-11-07_round6-decomposition.md#re-partition-operator-q-2026-11-07)). It carries no implementation, research, participant or publication evidence. Written 2026-11-07T03:42:36Z with the [partition plan](2026-11-07_round6-decomposition.md), revised 2026-11-07T04:19:14Z, regenerated 2026-11-07T04:49:42Z. Supplement: [`docs/experiments-spec.md`](../../experiments-spec.md), canonical v0.3, sha256 `4329b2740fe6be0ff80be585388bae63e1802ed34740478ba4a37d9d03e78531`; pattern `REQ-X[A-H]-[0-9]+`. The id source is spec Appendix A (REQ-XH-003). The machine-readable companion is [`2026-11-07_round6-coverage.json`](2026-11-07_round6-coverage.json) (schema `hh-supplement-plan/1`: the round-5 precedent's fields with the values its retained checks recompute, plus the additive fields below).

There are 456 candidates: 370 adopted (338 source + 32 synthesis-allocated), 81 merged-with and 5 superseded-by aliases. Each adopted id has exactly one primary owner row. Each alias inherits its target's owner, and the target keeps the alias's literal predicate bytes (`literal_row`, verbatim from its source note). Scope: 336 adopted ids are first-pass; 34 are routed (22 to Round 7 and 12 to Round 8), with CAP6.2 (the closure capstone) writing their routing record and re-reading it live before GATE-ACCEPT. By owner kind: ticket 319, capstone 39 (CAP6.2: 34 routed + 5 closure), skeleton 9, gate 2, human 1. The re-partition moved no id between deliverables except in the tail: every merged row owns the union of its former rows' ids, the five folded record-only rows owned none, and the former CAP6.1 (34), CAP6.3 (2), REC6.1 (2) and REC6.2 (1) ids are CAP6.2's.

## Register shape (what R6.1 consumes; SR-3 option (a))

Every candidate row carries every field below, with no null or empty-string value (`contributors` is a list; empty means "primary only").

| field | content | check it serves |
|---|---|---|
| `literal_row` | verbatim source-row bytes: the research/design note row for the 424 source ids; the spec's own normative `\| **REQ-…** \|` row for the 32 synthesis-allocated ids (`literal_source: docs/experiments-spec.md`) | alias-predicate "literal row present" |
| `source_sha256` | `sha256(literal_row)`, per row | alias-predicate "literal_row sha256 matches" (the retained guard's recompute) |
| `literal_source`, `literal_source_sha256` | the source file and its whole-file digest | frozen-source provenance; verbatim-in-source check |
| `requirement`, `acceptance` | adopted: the spec's normative and acceptance cells; alias: its own literal predicate (and literal acceptance, else the target's, labelled) | "requirement text is empty" |
| `appendix_a_row`, `appendix_a_row_sha256` | the verbatim Appendix A line | id source (the frozen spec has no per-id anchors) |
| `target_spec_row_sha256` | sha256 of the target's normative row in the spec | per-row digest of the frozen predicate |
| `spec_anchor` | an existing spec `<a id>`: `s0`…`s10`, `s0-4`, `s10-1` (every §10.1.x → `s10-1`) | § hook anchors |
| `ac_hook`, `ac_hook_resolution`, `hooks` | the verbatim Appendix A hook (`AC-<§ path>-<n>`), resolved `appendix-a-row`: by (id, hook) equality with the pinned Appendix A row, and present in the target's acceptance cell | AC-hook anchors (pattern widened to `AC-\d+(\.\d+)*-\d+` by R6.1) |
| `primary`, `primary_kind`, `primary_file`, `acceptance_anchor` | one chain row; its contract file; `ac-<chain id lowercased, dots → dashes>-<target id lowercased>`, an `<a id>` the Phase-3 contract writer places at the numbered AC | owner, ac-anchor |
| `contributors`, `round_scope`, `status` | owed-evidence rows (never dispatch dependencies); `first-pass` or `routed(round-7\|round-8)`; plan status | owner, routing |

R6.1's scope parametrizes the retained guard's per-source constants (coverage file, `REQ-X[A-H]-[0-9]+` pattern, 456/370/81/5 counts), resolves ids from Appendix A rather than `id="req-…"` anchors, and resolves AC hooks through `ac_hook_resolution`; it reuses the retained checks, never a second checker (CC1).

## Completion and owner rules

A row owns a bounded deliverable. A requirement is satisfied only when **all** its predicates, its aliases' literal predicates included, have evidence at the required layer (D/E/R/P, §0.2). An E pass is never an R or P pass, and an unexecuted study is unmet, not null.

- **O1 (default):** the primary owner is the row that produces the deliverable the requirement's acceptance hook inspects (code, schema, document, packet). Where a requirement spans a seam, the owner is the seam row that completes it, and the earlier row is a contributor (REQ-XC-330 → R6.23 with R6.22 contributing; REQ-XB-104 → R6.16 with R6.8 contributing).
- **O2 (skeleton owners):** an R- or P-layer id whose inspected record *is* a paid or provisioning window's own record is owned by that window's skeleton row, and is **owed at fleshing**. These are the W1 re-proof packet (REQ-XB-125, REQ-XH-116), the W2 stage packet (REQ-XD-041, REQ-XH-010) and the W3 L1 gate-run packet (REQ-XD-107, REQ-XE-006…009). Fleshing rewrites the skeleton row in place (kind skeleton → ticket, same id), so the ownership carries over unchanged. After the re-partition each skeleton also holds its window's ARCHIVE-UPLOAD act (W1's inside W2's skeleton) and, for W2 and W4, SETTLE; those acts own no adopted id. No D- or E-layer id is owned by a skeleton.
- **O3 (marker owners):** a gate or HUMAN row owns an id only when the id is literally a gate-readout or HUMAN obligation. GATE-G26 FP-S owns REQ-XH-007 (credit-period readout fields) and REQ-XH-013 (exclusivity acknowledgement at each paid gate), with GATE-G30 as contributor. HUMAN-H16 (formerly HUMAN-H23) owns REQ-XD-071 ("a HUMAN row SHALL review every flagged pass").
- **O4 (later-pass scope):** an adopted id with no Round-6 implementing obligation (§10.6, §10.1.6, §1.2) is owned by **CAP6.2** (the closure capstone), which writes its later-pass routing record (target round, trigger gate, withheld claim) before GATE-G32 signs and creates no implementing row (REQ-XH-001). CAP6.2 re-reads the register live in the same row (the operator's 3-run tail has no REC rows).
- **O5 (contributors):** each contributor row names evidence the owner relies on, such as live legs, window records or downstream packets. A contributor never becomes a dispatch dependency, and the owner's AC names exactly what is owed. Contract writers create the anchor `ac-<chain id, dots → dashes>-<req id>` in the owner contract for every owned id, as the literal owner table links it.

## Machine check

The register was checked by an independent script (v3: the Phase-4 v2 checks, SR-23, extended for the operator's re-partition). It reads only the spec (Appendix A, normative rows, `<a id>` anchors), the literal sources the JSON cites, the JSON, this file's literal owner table and owner index, and the decomposition's row table, Totals table, shared-decision table and linearization-B′ marker; it never reads the generator's data, and every check is isolated, so a missing id or malformed field prints a FAIL line instead of a traceback. v3 replaces the `tail=full` and two-guard-row checks with the minimal tail (capstone, capstone, gate, docs) and the single guard row R6.1, raises the size ceiling to 95k + 10k with an `operator-ruled` exception allowed only on a tail capstone, and adds the implement-spec band (40–50), the record-only-row fold and the B′ permutation checks; the owner-kind and routed-owner rules follow the renumbered HUMAN-H16 and the closure capstone CAP6.2. The script is committed at [`docs/build/tools/check_round6_coverage.py`](../tools/check_round6_coverage.py) (sha256 `057501644a8aca0d1a11c5b0c1f7c03d6c5bab95c9646c3eee70a1268b4f6b55`; v2 was `c08de6b6200e06b3f74644655b5fdc4b3d406663ebdd88b5a1d7d880e57b2694`); R6.1 folds it into the guard's legs (REQ-XH-003). **Retained-guard compatibility (SR-3).** The retained `Guard.check_candidate` (`docs/build/tools/supplement_guard.py`) was re-run in-process after the re-partition over all 456 candidates, with the re-partitioned plan's 73 row ids as `manifest_ids` and the spec's anchors: 0 `alias-predicate`, `disposition`, `layer` or `ac-anchor` errors; the only errors are 456 × `owner: primary_file … missing`, because the Phase-3 contract files do not exist yet. Its `REQ-[A-H]` alias regex and `AC-\d+-\d+` hook regex do not match the REQ-X spellings, so those two checks are skipped rather than passed; R6.1 widens them.

The re-partition generator's own checks agreed: every edge backward-only, the HUMAN placement rule under linearization A and B′, and per-row owner equality between the regenerated row table and the register. GUARD-X (R6.1) turns these into retained `hh-supplement-guard/1` legs (REQ-XH-002, REQ-XH-003). R6.1's contract also carries the pre-existing 46 legacy `reqcov` `unexplained-diagnostic` warnings as an OPEN FINDING, classified into the reviewed baseline with dated provenance, never silently (hand-off §4; coordinator ruling on SR-2).
